conclusion.justification: The report concludes that strong evidence supports the claim, stating dexamethasone improves survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring respiratory support.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** Yes—strong evidence shows that dexamethasone, a corticosteroid, improves survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients who require oxygen or mechanical ventilation, though it does not guarantee survival for every individual and offers no benefit for patients not needing respiratory support.

**Key evidence:**

- The **RECOVERY trial** (a large randomized controlled trial) found that dexamethasone 6 mg daily for up to 10 days reduced 28-day mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients receiving respiratory support. Mortality was reduced by roughly one-third among ventilated patients and one-fifth among those receiving oxygen only; no benefit was seen in patients not requiring oxygen.  
  https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

- **BMJ** reported the preliminary RECOVERY results, noting low-dose dexamethasone cut deaths in ventilated patients and reduced deaths by one-fifth in patients receiving oxygen only, with no benefit among those not needing respiratory support.  
  https://www.bmj.com/content/369/bmj.m2422

- The **WHO** welcomed the results, stating dexamethasone “can be lifesaving for patients who are critically ill with COVID-19.”  
  https://www.who.int/news/item/16-06-2020-who-welcomes-preliminary-results-about-dexamethasone-use-in-treating-critically-ill-covid-19-patients

- The **WHO Q&A** further notes corticosteroids are “lifesaving medicines recommended for patients with severe or critical COVID-19.”  
  https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-dexamethasone

Thus, the evidence supports your answer: dexamethasone improves survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients needing oxygen or ventilation, but it is not an absolute guarantee of survival.
